title: Parsing a raw HTTP request
description:
Parse a webhook delivery as it arrives on the wire (lesson 4.04), so nothing a framework does is hidden from you.

```python
def parse_request(raw, max_body=1_000_000): ...     # -> (method, path, headers, body)
```

`raw` is `bytes`. Raise `ValueError` for anything malformed. The rules:

1. The **head** ends at the first `\r\n\r\n`; if there is none, the request is incomplete. Decode the head as `latin-1`.
2. The first line is the **request line**: exactly three parts separated by single spaces, the method, the path and a version starting with `HTTP/1.`.
3. Each following line is a **header** `Name: value`. A line without `:`, or with an empty name or a name containing spaces, is malformed. Names are returned in **lower case**; values have spaces around them removed. If a name appears more than once, the values are joined with `", "` in order.
4. If there is a `content-length` header, it must be digits, and not more than `max_body` (otherwise `ValueError`); the **body** is exactly that many bytes after the head, and if fewer bytes are there, the request is incomplete. Bytes after the body are ignored. Without `content-length`, the body is `b""`.
hints: Work on bytes for the body and on text for the head: find the end of the head in the bytes, decode only the head, and slice the body from the original bytes so it is never altered.
`line.partition(":")` splits at the first colon only, so a value such as `t=1,v1=ab` or a URL with `https:` keeps its own colons.
unitTests:
def request(head, body=b""):
    return head.replace("\n", "\r\n").encode("latin-1") + b"\r\n" + body

@test("a delivery")
def _():
    body = b'{"id":"evt_1","type":"order.paid","data":{"order":"o_42"}}'
    raw = request(f"POST /webhooks HTTP/1.1\nHost: hooks.example.org\nContent-Type: application/json\nContent-Length: {len(body)}\nWebhook-Signature: t=1,v1=ab\n", body)
    method, path, headers, got = parse_request(raw)
    check_eq((method, path, got), ("POST", "/webhooks", body))
    check_eq(headers, {"host": "hooks.example.org", "content-type": "application/json", "content-length": "58", "webhook-signature": "t=1,v1=ab"})

@test("headers in detail")
def _():
    raw = request("GET /x?a=1 HTTP/1.0\nX-Tag:  one \nx-tag: two\nEmpty:\n")
    method, path, headers, body = parse_request(raw)
    check_eq((method, path, body), ("GET", "/x?a=1", b""))
    check_eq(headers, {"x-tag": "one, two", "empty": ""})

@test("the body is exactly Content-Length bytes")
def _():
    raw = request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: 3\n", b"abcdef")
    check_eq(parse_request(raw)[3], b"abc")
    raw = request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: 0\n", b"zzz")
    check_eq(parse_request(raw)[3], b"")
    body = "é\r\n\r\n".encode("utf-8")
    raw = request(f"POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: {len(body)}\n", body)
    check_eq(parse_request(raw)[3], body)

@test("malformed requests")
def _():
    bad = [
        b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n",
        request("POST /  HTTP/1.1\n"),
        request("POST / HTTP/2\n"),
        request("POST /\n"),
        request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nNoColon\n"),
        request("POST / HTTP/1.1\n: value\n"),
        request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nBad Name: v\n"),
        request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: ten\n"),
        request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: -1\n"),
        request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: 10\n", b"short"),
    ]
    for raw in bad:
        check_raises(ValueError, parse_request, raw)

@test("a body limit")
def _():
    raw = request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: 2000000\n", b"x")
    check_raises(ValueError, parse_request, raw)
    raw = request("POST / HTTP/1.1\nContent-Length: 5\n", b"12345")
    check_raises(ValueError, parse_request, raw, max_body=4)
    check_eq(parse_request(raw, max_body=5)[3], b"12345")
